# From Zenject

Use these tables to translate a Zenject or Extenject project. The binding vocabulary carries over:
`Bind<TContract>().To<TConcrete>().AsSingle()`, `[Inject]` on members, `MonoInstaller`,
`ProjectContext`, `SceneContext` and `GameObjectContext` all exist in Onity with the same roles. Five
behaviors differ and are worth reading before the tables: Onity is last-binding-wins instead of throwing
on a duplicate bind; it selects the public constructor with the most parameters (or the single `[Inject]`
constructor) instead of the fewest; it detects circular dependencies at resolve time; its `AsScoped()`
is a lifetime, not a sub-container; and signals are replaced by the messaging pillar. Everything in
these tables is verified against the Onity 0.7.0 source; an API that is not listed does not exist.

## Binding

| Zenject | Onity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().AsSingle()` | `container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().AsSingle()` | Identical. One instance in the declaring scope. |
| `Container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().AsTransient()` | `container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().AsTransient()` | A new instance per resolve. |
| `Container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().AsCached()` | `container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().AsSingle()` | There is no separate cached lifetime. |
| `Container.Bind<Foo>().AsSingle()` (self-bind) | `container.Bind<Foo>().AsSingle()` | `To` defaults to the contract type. |
| `Container.Bind<Foo>().ToSelf().FromNew().AsSingle()` | `container.Bind<Foo>().AsSingle()` | The `ToSelf` and `FromNew` ceremony has no counterpart. |
| `Container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().AsSingle().NonLazy()` | `container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().AsSingle().NonLazy()` | Created at `Build()`. `NonLazy()` before the lifetime throws `OnityBindingException`. |
| `Container.BindInstance(foo)` | `container.BindInstance<IFoo>(foo)` | Caller-owned. A null instance throws `OnityBindingException`. |
| `Container.BindInterfacesTo<Foo>().AsSingle()` | `container.BindInterfacesTo<Foo>().AsSingle()` | One instance under every interface; the concrete type is not bound. Throws when `Foo` has no interfaces. |
| `Container.BindInterfacesAndSelfTo<Foo>().AsSingle()` | `container.BindInterfacesAndSelfTo<Foo>().AsSingle()` | One instance under the concrete type and every interface. |
| `Container.Bind(typeof(IA), typeof(IB)).To<C>().AsSingle()` | `container.BindInterfacesAndSelfTo<C>().AsSingle()` or `BindInterfacesTo<C>()` | No multi-type `Bind(typeof, typeof)` overload. Two separate binds would create two instances. |
| `Container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().WithId("x").AsSingle()` | `container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().WithId("x").AsSingle()` | Ids compare by value. Call `WithId` before the lifetime. |
| `Container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().WhenInjectedInto<Bar>()` | `container.Bind<IFoo>().To<Foo>().WhenInjectedInto<Bar>().AsSingle()` | The consumer type and its derived types. Two matching conditions throw `OnityResolveException`; `WhenNotInjectedInto` has no counterpart. |
| `Container.Bind<IFoo>().FromSubContainerResolve().ByInstaller<FooInstaller>()` | `container.Bind<IFoo>().FromSubContainerResolve(scope => { ... })` | The installer is a delegate that binds `IFoo` inside the child; see [Sub-container exports](../guide/dependency-injection.md#sub-container-exports). |
| `Container.Unbind<IFoo>()` | `container.Unbind<IFoo>()`, `Unbind<IFoo>(id)` | Removes the local bindings, also after `Build()`. |
| `Container.Rebind<IFoo>().To<Foo2>().AsSingle()` | `container.Rebind<IFoo>().To<Foo2>().AsSingle()` | Replaces the local binding when the lifetime is selected. |
| Duplicate `Bind<Foo>().AsSingle()` throws | `container.Bind<Foo>().AsSingle()` twice: the last binding wins | Divergence. Nothing throws. |

Zenject's scoping through sub-containers maps to a lifetime: `AsScoped()` creates one instance per
resolving scope, so a `GameObjectContext` or child container that resolves a parent's scoped binding
gets its own instance. See [Lifetimes](../guide/lifecycle-and-scopes.md#lifetimes).

## Injection

`Onity.DI.InjectAttribute` targets constructors, fields, properties, methods and parameters, and has
one property, `Id`.

| Zenject | Onity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Constructor injection | Constructor injection | Identical and preferred. |
| `[Inject] public Foo(IBar bar)` | `[Inject] public Foo(IBar bar)` | A single `[Inject]` constructor wins over the others. |
| Several constructors: the one with the fewest arguments | Several constructors: the public one with the most parameters | Divergence. A non-public constructor is used only when no public one exists. |
| `[Inject] IClock m_clock;` | `[Inject] private IClock m_clock;` | Field injection, private allowed. Static members are never injected. |
| `[Inject] public ILogger Logger { get; set; }` | `[Inject] public ILogger Logger { get; set; }` | A setter is required; a get-only or indexer property throws `OnityBindingException`. |
| `[Inject] void Init(IConfig config)` | `[Inject] private void Init(IConfig config)` | Runs after the constructor, fields and properties. Cannot be generic. |
| `[Inject(Id = "x")] IFoo m_foo;` | `[Inject(Id = "x")] private IFoo m_foo;` | Also on properties and on individual constructor or method parameters. |
| `[Inject(Optional = true)]` | none | Bind the dependency, or use `TryResolve` in glue code. |
| `Container.Inject(existing)` | `container.Inject(existing)` | Member-injects an existing object. A null target throws `OnityResolveException`. |
| `Container.InjectGameObject(root)` | `context.InjectGameObject(root)` | On the owning `OnityContext`; it skips objects owned by a nearer context. |

Member injection order is base class, then derived class; within a type fields, then properties, then
methods.

## Resolution

| Zenject | Onity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Container.Resolve<IFoo>()` | `container.Resolve<IFoo>()` | Throws `OnityResolveException` when unresolvable. |
| `Container.Resolve(typeof(IFoo))` | `container.Resolve(typeof(IFoo))` | Runtime-type form. |
| `Container.ResolveId<IFoo>("x")` | `container.Resolve<IFoo>("x")` | Identified resolve; `Resolve(Type, id)` for the runtime-type form. |
| `Container.TryResolve<IFoo>()` (null on miss) | `container.TryResolve<IFoo>(out IFoo foo)` | Returns `bool`; the identified form is `TryResolve<IFoo>("x", out foo)`. |
| `Container.HasBinding<IFoo>()` | `container.CanResolve(typeof(IFoo))` | No construction. |
| `Container.ResolveAll<IFoo>()` | `container.Resolve<IReadOnlyList<IFoo>>()` | Or `IEnumerable<IFoo>`, `IReadOnlyCollection<IFoo>`, `IList<IFoo>`, `ICollection<IFoo>`, `List<IFoo>`, `IFoo[]`. There is no `ResolveAll` method. |
| `DiContainer` injected into a class | `IResolver` or `OnityContainer` | Both resolve to the active scope; inject `IResolver` in a factory. |

## Factories

Onity has no fluent factory body and no generated placeholder factory. You author an `IFactory<...>`
(`Onity.Factory`) and bind it with `BindFactory`; the factory is bound with
`BindInterfacesAndSelfTo<TFactory>().AsSingle()`.

| Zenject | Onity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Container.BindFactory<Foo, Foo.Factory>()` | `container.BindFactory<Foo, FooFactory>()` where `FooFactory : IFactory<Foo>` | Resolve `IFactory<Foo>` and call `Create()`. |
| `Container.BindFactory<string, Foo, Foo.Factory>()` | `container.BindFactory<string, Foo, FooFactory>()` where `FooFactory : IFactory<string, Foo>` | Resolve `IFactory<string, Foo>` and call `Create(id)`. |
| Two-argument factory | `container.BindFactory<string, int, Foo, FooFactory>()` where `FooFactory : IFactory<string, int, Foo>` | Two parameters is the largest arity; wrap more in a struct. |
| `PlaceholderFactory<T>` subclass | a hand-written `IFactory<...>` class | The factory takes services in its constructor and builds the value itself. |
| `BindMemoryPool<Foo, Foo.Pool>()`, `MonoMemoryPool` | `BindPooledFactory(prefab, parent, defaultCapacity, maxSize)`; `OnityObjectPool<T>` for plain objects | Binds `IPool<T>` and `IFactory<T>`. Reset logic goes in `IPoolHooks`. See [Factories and Pooling](../guide/factories-and-pooling.md). |
| `OnSpawned` and `OnDespawned` | `IPoolHooks.OnPoolGet()` and `OnPoolRelease()` | On the pooled component. |
| `Container.Instantiate<Foo>(args)` | none | Author an `IFactory<TParam, TValue>`. |

```csharp
using Onity.Factory;            // IFactory<TParam, TValue>

public sealed class EnemyFactory : IFactory<EnemySpawnRequest, Enemy>
{
    private readonly IClock m_clock;

    public EnemyFactory(IClock clock)   // services come through the constructor
    {
        m_clock = clock;
    }

    public Enemy Create(EnemySpawnRequest request)
    {
        return new Enemy(request.Id, request.Level, m_clock);
    }
}
```

Bind and use (fragment): `container.BindFactory<EnemySpawnRequest, Enemy, EnemyFactory>();`
then `container.Resolve<IFactory<EnemySpawnRequest, Enemy>>().Create(request)`.

## Automatic lifecycle

In Zenject you bind the type and rely on `BindInterfacesAndSelfTo` to expose the lifecycle interfaces. In
Onity, binding a singleton, a scoped binding or a bound instance that implements a lifecycle interface
(`Onity.DI`) is enough; the container collects it at `Build()`, and the owning context pumps the ticks.
Transients are not collected.

| Zenject | Onity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IInitializable.Initialize()` | `IOnityInitializable.Initialize()` | Once, at the end of `Build()`, in binding-registration order. |
| `ITickable.Tick()` | `IOnityTickable.Tick()` | From the context's `Update`. |
| `IFixedTickable.FixedTick()` | `IOnityFixedTickable.FixedTick()` | From `FixedUpdate`. |
| `ILateTickable.LateTick()` | `IOnityLateTickable.LateTick()` | From `LateUpdate`. |
| async startup through a UniTask method | `IOnityAsyncInitializable.InitializeAsync(CancellationToken)` | Awaited in `BuildAsync`, which a context runs from `Start`. See [Async initialization](../guide/lifecycle-and-scopes.md#async-initialization). |
| `IDisposable` on a bound singleton | `IDisposable` on a bound singleton | Disposed with the scope, after the scope token is canceled. |
| `IGuiRenderable`, `IPoolable` | none | Draw from a `MonoBehaviour`; use `IPoolHooks` for pooled components. |

```csharp
using Onity.DI;                 // IOnityInitializable, IOnityTickable

public sealed class WaveDirector : IOnityInitializable, IOnityTickable
{
    public void Initialize()
    {
        // Runs once at Build(), in registration order.
    }

    public void Tick()
    {
        // Runs every Update from the owning context.
    }
}
```

Binding it is the whole wiring (fragment): `container.BindInterfacesAndSelfTo<WaveDirector>().AsSingle();`.

## Collection injection

Bind several implementations of one contract, then inject the set. The set is gathered from every
explicit binding in this scope and its ancestors, ancestors first. Fragment:

```csharp
container.Bind<IDamageRule>().To<CritRule>().AsSingle();
container.Bind<IDamageRule>().To<ArmorRule>().AsSingle();
```

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;

public sealed class DamagePipeline
{
    private readonly IReadOnlyList<IDamageRule> m_rules;

    public DamagePipeline(IReadOnlyList<IDamageRule> rules)   // Zenject: List<IDamageRule>
    {
        m_rules = rules;
    }
}
```

A plain `Resolve<IDamageRule>()` returns the last binding, so single-resolve call sites keep working;
only a collection-typed request gathers all of them.

## Open generic bindings

Bind an open generic definition once; any closed form resolves on demand and is cached as a normal
binding (fragment):

```csharp
container.Bind(typeof(IRepository<>)).To(typeof(Repository<>)).AsSingle();
IRepository<PlayerProfile> profiles = container.Resolve<IRepository<PlayerProfile>>();
```

`NonLazy()` is not supported on an open generic binding. On IL2CPP the closed type must survive
stripping.

## Scopes and contexts

| Zenject | Onity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ProjectContext` prefab in `Resources` | `ProjectContext` prefab at `Assets/Resources/Onity/ProjectContext.prefab` | Create it with `Onity/Contexts/Create ProjectContext Prefab`; loaded before the first scene. |
| `SceneContext` | `SceneContext` (`Onity.Unity.Contexts`) | Child of the `ProjectContext` when one exists. |
| `GameObjectContext` | `GameObjectContext` | Child of the nearest context above it, else the `ProjectContext`. |
| `MonoInstaller.InstallBindings()` using `Container` | `MonoInstaller.InstallBindings(OnityContainer container)` (`Onity.Unity.Installers`) | The container is a parameter. |
| `ScriptableObjectInstaller` | `BindScriptableObject(asset)` inside a `MonoInstaller` | Member-injects the asset and binds it as an instance. |
| `Container.CreateSubContainer()` | `new OnityContainer(parent)` | A child inherits the parent's bindings; a child binding shadows the parent only inside the child. |
| Sub-container facade | `FromSubContainerResolve(install)` | Exports one contract from a child installed per requesting scope. |
| `Container.Dispose()` or scene unload | `container.Dispose()`; a context disposes in `OnDestroy` | Cancels the scope token, then disposes child scopes, scoped instances and singletons in reverse registration order. |
| none | `container.Build()`, `await container.BuildAsync(token)` | A context calls both. Build callbacks cannot be registered after the build. |

Every context binds the container, `IResolver`, `IOnityScopeLifetime`, the context, `MessageBroker`
and `OnityEventHub`, so these need no installer line.

## Signals and messaging

Zenject signals map to the messaging pillar. There is no signal installer and no declaration step: the
broker is bound by every context, and any struct or class is a message.

| Zenject | Onity | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SignalBusInstaller.Install(Container)` | none | Every context binds `MessageBroker` and `OnityEventHub`. |
| `Container.DeclareSignal<T>()` | none, or `container.BindMessageChannel<T>()` | Bind the channel only when a service injects `IPublisher<T>` or `ISubscriber<T>` alone. |
| `SignalBus.Fire(signal)` | `OnityEventHub.Publish(message)` in services; `OnityEvent.Publish(this, message)` in MonoBehaviours | `OnityEventHub` is in `Onity.Unity.Messaging`, `OnityEvent` in `Onity.Unity`. |
| `SignalBus.Subscribe<T>(handler)` and `Unsubscribe` | `OnityEventHub.Subscribe<T>(handler).AddTo(scope)`; `OnityEvent.Subscribe<T>(this, handler)` | Subscriptions are `IDisposable`; retain them with `AddTo(scope)`, `AddTo(this)` or `TakeUntilDisable(this)`. The owner overload of `OnityEvent.Subscribe` disposes on destroy. |
| `SignalBus.GetStream<T>()` | `OnityEventHub.Observe<T>()`; `OnityEvent.Observe<T>(this)` | An `IOnityObservable<T>`; apply `Where`, `Select` and the other operators. |
| `Container.BindSignal<T>().ToMethod(...)` | a subscription in the handler's constructor, retained with `AddTo(scope)` | See [Events and Messaging](../guide/events-messaging.md). |

## Errors

Onity has two DI exception types in `Onity.DI`. `OnityResolveException` covers resolve and inject
failures: unbound contracts, circular dependencies, failed construction, ambiguous conditional bindings,
null targets and use after dispose. `OnityBindingException` covers configuration failures: null or
non-assignable implementations, `BindInterfacesTo` on a type without interfaces, multiple `[Inject]`
constructors, setterless, indexer or generic `[Inject]` members, callbacks registered after build, and
`NonLazy` before a lifetime. Map a `ZenjectException` catch onto these two.

## Not supported

These Zenject features have no Onity counterpart. Use the replacement.

| Zenject feature | Do this in Onity |
| --- | --- |
| `Container.Instantiate<T>(args)` | Author an `IFactory<TParam, TValue>` and `BindFactory`. |
| Fluent factory bodies (`FromMethod`, `FromFactory`, `FromIFactory`) and generated `PlaceholderFactory` | Write the factory class. |
| `[Inject(Optional = true)]` | Bind the dependency, or `TryResolve` in glue code. |
| `BindInstance(null)` | Pass a non-null instance. |
| Signals (`SignalBus`, `DeclareSignal`, `BindSignal`) | Messaging: `OnityEventHub`, `OnityEvent`, `BindMessageChannel<T>`. |
| `WhenNotInjectedInto` and other condition forms | `WhenInjectedInto<TConsumer>()` only; otherwise distinct contract types or a factory. |
| Multi-type `Bind(typeof(IA), typeof(IB))` | `BindInterfacesAndSelfTo` or `BindInterfacesTo`. |
| `AsCached` as a distinct lifetime | `AsSingle()`. |
| `ResolveAll` | Request a collection type. |
| Duplicate-binding errors | Last binding wins; use `Rebind` when the replacement should be explicit. |

Features that ship and need no workaround: `AsScoped()`, `WithId`, `[Inject(Id = ...)]`,
`WhenInjectedInto`, `Unbind`, `Rebind`, `FromSubContainerResolve`, collection injection, open generic
bindings, the automatic lifecycle, and pools (`OnityObjectPool<T>`, `PrefabComponentPool<T>`,
`BindPooledFactory`).

## Lifetime and async

Zenject has no scope token and no awaitable startup of its own. In Onity every scope has a
`LifetimeToken` that is canceled before the scope disposes its services; services inject
`IOnityScopeLifetime` for it, MonoBehaviours call `GetScopeCancellationToken()`, and `IOnityAsyncInitializable`
with `OnityContext.WaitReadyAsync` replaces hand-written startup ordering. Read
[Lifecycle and Scopes](../guide/lifecycle-and-scopes.md) before you move startup code, and
[From UniTask](From-UniTask.md) if the project also uses UniTask.
